text:
yuan: quick RFC follow-up — re: multi-region topology. after the call with product/legal I sketched two options: active/active with region-scoped storage vs active/passive with synchronous failover. want pros/cons before I update the RFC.
ashley: +1, good to have this in thread. high level: active/active gives best latency but makes strict data residency and causal consistency harder. active/passive simpler for residency but worse p99.
mike: ops note: active/active will need strong failure isolation and circuit breakers. we can't rely on cross-region sync for requests during infra partition.
sarah: product constraint: some EU customers require that PII never leaves region and be deletable within 24h. that rules out dual-write to non-EU replicas unless encrypted + legal hold.
diego: legal: EU residency = data at rest within EU unless explicit contract. replication for DR is allowed if we can demonstrate contractual controls and encryption in transit+at rest, and if we can perform region-scoped deletes.
ops-jen: implementation idea: keep control-plane global but make storage region-scoped per-tenant. routing layer sends requests to tenant region by default. this avoids most dual-write problems.
yuan: that was my baseline: global routing + tenant->home-region sticky routing. fallback to nearest region only for availability and only after TTL for cached tokens. concerns: capacity skew and cross-region cache warmup.
ashley: tradeoffs:
- Latency: home-region gives best latency for most requests.
- Cost: extra cold-starts and cross-region cache fills add cost.
- Consistency: if we allow failover writes in another region we need idempotent/CRDT semantics or a single-write arbiter.
mike: on failover, we should consider a short-term "read-only" fallback mode for non-critical writes. e.g., if home region is down, route reads + queue writes for async materialization. that reduces correctness risks.
sre-bot: deploy-note: Canary for regional routing change requires traffic mirroring for 5% of requests for 30m, then 20% for 2h.
sarah: product wants configurable policies per-customer: (1) strict residency (no cross-region writes), (2) best-effort (reads allowed cross-region, writes queued), (3) performance-first (active/active).
diego: add a checkbox for customers to opt into cross-region replication with contract. treat as enterprise feature.
ashley: technical approaches to make active/active safer:
- store tenant data in region-bound DBs; replicate only metadata/global configs out-of-band.
- for cross-region writes, use a primary-election per-tenant using a lightweight lease service.
- or accept eventual consistency with conflict resolution (last-writer wins + vector clocks) for user-generated content that tolerates it.
yuan: sample lease sketch (pseudo):
```
acquire_lease(tenant_id):
  if lease.owner == region && lease.expires > now: fail
  else set owner=region, expires=now+ttl
```
writes only allowed if local region holds lease. on failure, queue write to owner's queue.
```

mike: leaning to per-tenant lease + queueing. simplest to reason about and matches residency needs. downside: extra latency when leader moves.
ops-jen: scaling note: we'll need a global index for lease lookup. can be small KV with replication but mustn't store tenant PII. store only tenant id -> lease metadata.
sarah: UX question: what should happen in UI when failover occurs? customers need clear notification and an option to switch to manual failover.
yuan: we can emit events: tenant.failover.start, tenant.failover.end and surface in Console + webhook.
diego: keep audit trail for any cross-region writes. that'll be required for compliance reviews.
nashley: performance suggestion: add read-replicas in nearest region for reads only, but ensure write path remains home-region (unless lease flips). reduces latency for heavy-read workloads.
mike: operational runbook additions: pre-warm KV caches after failover, drain queues, and run consistency checks. also we need metric (stale-reads) and alarms.
sre-bot: incident-template created: "regional-failover-playbook" (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/regional-failover)
yuan: next steps: I'll update RFC with two concrete patterns: (A) "home-region primary with queue-based failover" (default, supports residency), (B) "opt-in active/active with per-tenant lease + conflict resolution" (enterprise only). asking engineering + legal to review before EOD Thursday.
sarah: ack — product will prepare per-customer policy options.
diego: will draft the contract clause for opt-in replication.
ashley: engineering: I'll outline the lease service and housekeeping tasks. ping me if you want pairing on prototype.
mike: Ops will scope SLO changes and runbook updates.
ops-jen: I'll add traffic-mirroring tests to our chaos suite to exercise routing policy.
yuan: thanks all — I'll post updated RFC link here once it's in the repo.
